newsitem.title: UK: NWE barges up and down on bidding, low sulph stead.
newsitem.headline: NWE barges up and down on bidding, low sulph stead.

text.p: Buyers pushed up European high sulphur barge values early on Tuesday as swaps gathered strength on the back of crude's morning run, traders said.
But prices slipped back as the screen dipped after the NYMEX opened and the barge bidder ran out of buying energy.
Barges hit $87 fob ARA before slipping back, with the bulk of the day's limited trade done at $85.
"I think $82-$84 is the real range, where there is real demand and real offers," said one trader. "I think today's $87 was just a hiccup."
Low sulphur was supported by stronger swaps, up $2 at $89/$90 for May, but notional deal numbers were stuck at $87/$89. Recent deals were all on a floating basis.
"I think we might have reached the bottom on low sulphur but really it's a pretty poor market to be in," said one refiner. "You really need to have a contract to be sure you'll sell it."
Cargo availability into May was reported reasonable.
High sulphur cargoes were steady, with most dealers discounting the Portuguese state electricity company's May tender for 75,000 tonnes as unlikely to move the market.
The tender closes on Wednesday, with an announcement of results on Thursday.
